name: Devānanda Paṇḍita
text:
## In short

Devānanda Paṇḍita of Kuliyā, a famous and austere teacher of the *Bhāgavatam*, «a most peaceful brāhmaṇa who desired liberation» but without devotion; his students threw Śrīvāsa out of his class. The Lord rebuked him; later, by serving Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, he received the Lord's mercy and His teaching on the *Bhāgavatam*.

## Śrīvāsa thrown out (Madhya 9.90–96; 21.53–66)

Śrīvāsa once went to hear the *Bhāgavatam* from him; his heart melted, he cried and fell to the ground. «The sinful students there said, “This is a disturbance… we are unable to study”» — and dragged him out. «Devānanda Paṇḍita did not stop them. As the guru was devoid of devotional service, so were his students.» The Lord, as the Supersoul, knew.

The *bhāṣya* (21.57–58, 21.65): he was peaceful, with many good qualities, and from childhood kept a vow of celibacy like a sannyāsī — but without devotion that celibacy turned into aversion to the devotees' service; had he had the least inclination to the Lord's service he would have stopped his students.

## The Lord's rebuke (Madhya 21.5–78)

Wandering near the house of Viśārada Maheśvara (Sārvabhauma's father), the Lord heard him recite: «What kind of explanation can this fellow give?… Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the incarnation of Lord Kṛṣṇa in the form of a book… The four Vedas are like yogurt, and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is like butter… Anyone who discriminates between Me, My servant, and the book Bhāgavatam is certainly destroyed.» Meeting him later, the Lord remembered the offense to Śrīvāsa and chastised him: «O Devānanda… Is it proper to throw out someone who after hearing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is crying in love for Kṛṣṇa?» Devānanda felt ashamed and made no reply (21.75–78), and went home «distressed because of bad association» (22.5).

## Through Vakreśvara Paṇḍita (Antya 3.464–524)

After the Lord's sannyāsa, Devānanda «had the good fortune of meeting Vakreśvara Paṇḍita», who stayed some time in his āśrama. «As long as Vakreśvara Paṇḍita danced, Devānanda Paṇḍita would guard him with a stick in hand», keeping people away and catching him when he fell; thus he developed faith in Lord Caitanya and a desire to see Him. He came, offered obeisances and stood hesitantly in a corner. «The Lord excused all of Devānanda's previous offenses»: «You are able to see Me because you served Vakreśvara Paṇḍita… When Vakreśvara dances, Kṛṣṇa dances.»

Devānanda prayed: «I am an ignorant person yet I teach Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam… How should I explain it, and what should I teach?» The Lord answered: «In the beginning, middle, and end of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam devotional service to Viṣṇu is described… One who thinks, “I understand Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,” does not know the glories of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam… The Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is filled with ecstatic love. It is the body of Lord Kṛṣṇa.» Devānanda offered full obeisances and considered himself fortunate (3.524).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 9.90–96; 21.5–78; 22.4–6; Antya 3.464–524.

name: Govinda Ghoṣa
text:
## In short

Govinda Ghoṣa, the kīrtana leader, one of the three Ghoṣa brothers — «the singers of Vṛndāvana».

## In the book

- **Kīrtana groups** (Madhya 8.142): «Another group was headed by Govinda Ghoṣa. All the devotees chanted during the dancing of Gauracandra.»
- **With Nityānanda** (Antya 5.257–259): «Mādhava, Vāsudeva, and Govinda were three brothers. When they began to sing, Lord Nityānanda would dance.» The *bhāṣya*: they were not like ordinary mundane kīrtana singers; therefore they were called the singers of Vṛndāvana.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 8.142; Antya 5.257–259.

name: Nārāyaṇī Devī
text:
## In short

Nārāyaṇī, the little niece of Śrīvāsa (daughter of his brother), who received the Lord's remnants and cried in love of Kṛṣṇa at His order — the mother of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, the author of the *Caitanya-bhāgavata*.

## «Chant the name of Kṛṣṇa and cry» (Madhya 2.321–323)

«The Lord then looked at Śrīvāsa's niece, a small girl named Nārāyaṇī, standing before Him. Even today Nārāyaṇī is known among Vaiṣṇavas as the recipient of Lord Caitanya's remnants. Śrī Gaurāṅga, the Supersoul of all living entities, ordered her, “Nārāyaṇī, chant the name of Kṛṣṇa and cry.”»

## The Lord's remnants (Madhya 10.290–296)

«The fortunate Nārāyaṇī received the remnants left after the Lord finished eating. The innocent young girl Nārāyaṇī was the daughter of Śrīvāsa's brother. The Lord gave her His remnants.» Then He ordered her: «O Nārāyaṇī, let Me hear you cry in ecstasy for Kṛṣṇa» — and she was known as *gaurāṅgera avaśeṣa-pātra nārāyaṇī*, «Nārāyaṇī, the recipient of Gaurāṅga's remnants». (Ādi 1.150: such remnants are rarely attained even by Brahmā.)

## The author's mother (Antya 5.757–758)

> «The last of His servants is Vṛndāvana dāsa. He took birth from the womb of Nārāyaṇī, who was the recipient of the Lord's remnants. Even today the Vaiṣṇavas glorify Nārāyaṇī as the recipient of Lord Caitanya's remnants.»

The *bhāṣya*: Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura is not known by his father's line but by his relation with his mother, the devotee of Gaura who received the remnants of Śrī Caitanyadeva.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 1.150; Madhya 2.321–323; 10.290–296; Antya 5.757–758.

name: Vāsudeva Datta
text:
## In short

Vāsudeva Datta of Caṭṭagrāma, «the benefactor of the entire world»: the Lord said, «This body of Mine belongs to Vāsudeva alone.»

## Birth (Ādi 2.36–37)

«Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi, the topmost Vaiṣṇava, Caitanya-vallabha, and Vāsudeva Datta all appeared in Caṭṭagrāma.» The *bhāṣya*: he was born in the village of **Chāṅhārā**, near Paṭiyā police station in the district of Caṭṭagrāma, twenty miles from Mekhalā, Puṇḍarīka's birthplace.

## In Navadvīpa

«Only Mukunda and Vāsudeva Datta knew the glories of his [Puṇḍarīka's] ecstatic love» (Madhya 7.43). The book glorifies the Lord as «the dear Lord of Vāsudeva and Śrīgarbha» (9.5), «the benefactor of Haridāsa and Vāsudeva» (13.258), «the Lord of Gaṅgādāsa and Vāsudeva» (21.2).

## «I belong to Vāsudeva» (Antya 5.18–30)

When the Lord came back to Śrīvāsa's house after His sannyāsa, «Vāsudeva Datta and various other associates headed by Śivānanda Sena arrived there. Vāsudeva Datta was most dear to the Lord. By the Lord's mercy, he knew all conclusive truths… the benefactor of the entire world… compassionate to all living entities.» The Lord embraced him and cried; Vāsudeva grasped His feet and wept so that even hearts like dry wood or stone were moved.

> e śarīra vāsudeva dattera āmāra

«“Vāsudeva Datta may sell Me wherever he likes. This is a fact… One who is touched by air that has touched the body of Vāsudeva Datta will always be protected by Kṛṣṇa. Listen, O Vaiṣṇavas, I tell you the truth! This body of Mine belongs to Vāsudeva alone.”» (5.26–30)

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 2.36–37; Madhya 7.43, 9.5, 13.258, 21.2; Antya 5.18–30.

name: Gopīnātha Siṁha
text:
## In short

Gopīnātha Siṁha, whom the Lord used to call «Akrūra».

## In the book

> calilena gopīnātha siṁha mahāśaya
> akrūra kariyā yāṅre gauracandra kaya

«Śrī Gopīnātha Siṁha also came. Lord Gauracandra would address him as Akrūra.» (Antya 8.35, the devotees going to Purī; the *bhāṣya* refers to *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 10.76.)

(The *Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā* 117 — quoted in his «Gaṇoddeśa» — also makes him Akrūra.)

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Antya 8.35.
